valuation.method: Forward EPS x P/E: FY2027 adjusted diluted EPS (fiscal year ending Jan 2028) viewed at the 12-month target date (Nov 2027), using only information public by the 2026-11-13 close. Anchored on FY2026 guidance (Q2 release 2026-08-19) of adjusted EPS about $12.25, sales about $92B, flat comps; Q2 adjusted EPS $4.40 incl. $0.11 tariff refund benefit, comps +0.2%. USD US listing, no ADR conversion. Q3 release after the close is excluded. Multiples are judgment-based, not sourced.

bear.driver: Housing turnover stays frozen, comps negative, FBM/ADG integration and margin pressure; EPS roughly flat to below FY2026 guide

base.driver: Flat to low-single-digit comps, Pro/FBM contribution and buybacks give about 8% EPS growth off a tariff-refund-flattered base

bull.driver: Lower mortgage rates lift turnover and big-ticket demand, comps +3%, margin leverage

valuation.implied_by_close: At base EPS $13.20 the close implies 17.3x; the average of the five named targets (about $236) implies 17.9x on base EPS, or about $11.8 EPS at 20x
valuation.sensitivity: One turn of P/E moves the base target by $13.20 (5.8 pp of the close)
valuation.watch_metric: Comparable sales and operating margin, with FY2026 guide of flat comps and adjusted EPS about $12.25
valuation.next_disclosure: Q3 FY2026 results, 2026-11-19 (approx.); Q4 and fiscal 2026 results expected February 2027

analyst_notes: Named calls are sparse and dated mostly to the Q2 release: Mizuho cut to $250 from $280 while KeyBanc ($275), RBC ($231) and TD Cowen ($235) held. Stifel downgraded to Sell at $190 ahead of Q3. The spread of $190-$275 is wide; the base case sits near the middle, requiring about 8% EPS growth at 20x. Targets have no documented 12-month horizon and the Stifel date is inferred from a Thursday reference, so none is weighted.
